title: Garlic Lemon Chicken with Green Beans and Sweet Potato Mash
description: Skin-on chicken thighs roasted in a garlic, lemon, and chili marinade, served with lemon garlic green beans and a lightened sweet potato mash.

ingredients.name: boneless, skin-on chicken thighs, about 1.75 lb (chicken)
salt, divided, plus pepper (green beans and mash)

instructions.text: Whisk the ginger, garlic, chili flakes, herbs, onion powder, honey, olive oil, lemon juice, and salt. Toss with the thighs, working some under the skin. Marinate at least 30 minutes, or up to several hours in the fridge.
Heat the oven to 400°F convection (425°F conventional). Place the thighs skin side up on a sheet pan or in a baking dish.
Roast 25 to 30 minutes until the thickest part reads 175°F. Air fryer: 375°F for 18 to 22 minutes, skin side up.
Put the sweet potatoes in a pot of salted water. Boil 15 to 20 minutes until fork-tender.
Drain the sweet potatoes, reserving 1/2 cup of the water. Off the heat, mash with the yogurt, olive oil, and enough cooking water to get smooth. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Cook the green beans 4 to 6 minutes until crisp-tender. Add the garlic for the last 30 seconds, then finish with the lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Rest the chicken 5 minutes. Peel off the skin before eating and discard it and the pan drippings. Serve over the mash with the beans.

notes:
Peeling the skin and leaving out the drippings removes most of the saturated fat. The original used about 40g of butter between the beans and mash, which the olive oil and yogurt replace.

If the chicken is dry, rest it longer or spoon a little lemon juice over it. Don't use the drippings.

Mash options: sweet potato is the original and the sweetest. Two lower-carb or lower-limit alternatives:

Butternut squash: about 12g carbs per 100g raw versus about 20g for sweet potato, so it is the lowest-carb option, and it is on Jen's good list. Use 1.5 lb peeled, cubed squash (about 4 cups). Roast at 400°F for 30 to 35 minutes for the best flavor, or boil 12 to 15 minutes. Drain very well. If it looks watery, return it to the dry pot over low heat for a minute. Mash with the yogurt and olive oil, using less cooking water than the recipe says, since squash is softer.

Yukon Gold: on Jen's good list, with a creamier texture and more potassium and vitamin C than sweet potato. The carbs are similar to sweet potato, so don't expect a big glucose benefit. Use 1.5 lb peeled, chopped potatoes and boil 15 to 20 minutes until fork-tender. Mash as written.

Adaptation: the original used sweet potato, butter, and milk. This version swaps the butter and milk for olive oil and yogurt. The marinade and green bean steps are inferred, since the original caption listed only ingredients and chicken cook times.
